recommendations.name: The M6 and M5 Pro Mac Mini
recommendations.blurb: Apple updated its tiny computer this week, and you can preorder it with a new M6 chip or an M5 Pro. Unfortunately, they have starting prices that are $100 more expensive than the previous generation, and the new model won’t be released until September 22nd.

recommendations.name: Star Wars: Zero Company
recommendations.blurb: This strategy game set in the Star Wars universe has been getting rave reviews. Gotta find some time to squeeze this in with all of the other big games coming out soon.

recommendations.name: HMD’s Nokia 300 Charge
recommendations.blurb: HMD made an old-school, candybar-style Nokia dumbphone that doubles as a power bank. It also has a 3.5mm headphone jack. Who needs a foldable iPhone when you can have this?

recommendations.name: Wyze’s Indoor Cam Pan
recommendations.blurb: This new $39.98 security camera can tilt 360 degrees around and 103 degrees vertically, but it also has a privacy mode that tilts the lens fully downward into the body of the camera so that it can’t see anything. Great feature.

recommendations.name: Garmin’s Fenix 9 smartwatches
recommendations.blurb: The Fenix 9 and 9 Pro have OLED screens, 64GB of storage, and for the two bigger sizes of the 9 Pro, the option to get solar-charging displays. The watches aren’t cheap, though: The Fenix 9 starts at $999.99, while the Pro starts at $1,099.99.

recommendations.name: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition
recommendations.blurb: The Switch 2 version of FromSoftware’s all-time classic is apparently worth the wait after a big delay. Do I need yet another excuse to get lost in The Lands Between? Probably not, but I’m tempted.

recommendations.name: Whoop’s Meridian Band
recommendations.blurb: This $149 band is made from Milanese mesh, comes in gold, rose gold, silver, and black, and makes your fifth-gen Whoop tracker look super fancy. But one part isn’t so fancy: You can’t charge your Whoop while it’s in the Meridian Band.

recommendations.blurb: The phone: iPhone 17 Pro, deep blue, 1 TB (of which only 200 GB is used, but that won’t stop me from wasting money on a 1 TB model this year too).

recommendations.name: It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia
recommendations.blurb: Third, It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia, whose 18th season just started; it’s the best and most realistic show set in Philadelphia ever made.

recommendations.name: A la Card
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been playing A la Card and REALLY enjoying my time with it. It’s an indie roguelike deck builder game that feels like Slay the Spire and Balatro said ‘Let’s go out for food from a food truck.’ All cards can be mutated and changed via the events — their values, their effect, what triggers them.

recommendations.name: Emo Revival
recommendations.blurb: My preorder shipped early so I’ve been reading Emo Revival by Andrew Sacher and it’s a 10/10 so far.

recommendations.name: House of Guinness
recommendations.blurb: Tonight I’m going to finish House of Guinness. It’s a fine show but even better if you drink when watching it.

recommendations.name: Berserker
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been on a kick reading older sci-fi novels recently and came across Berserker by Fred Saberhagen (1967). Fantastic book but surprisingly hard to find a physical copy. Ended up purchasing an ePub. Highly recommend!
